name: bruna-go-live-busy
title: Bruna's go-live, busier: the same history and questions, with 81 more ordinary statements
source: Pablo Piovano, three-memories-one-question (MIT), scenarios/go-live.json at commit 485fff9; the 81 statements in the sessions of Sep 14, Sep 28, Oct 12, Oct 19, Nov 2, Nov 16, Nov 23, Nov 30 and Dec 2 were added for AgentMemory, so the store outgrows the judge's 50 candidates
assistantBrief: You are the personal assistant of Bruna, a tech lead.

messages: Hi! I'm Bruna, tech lead at Nexo, a small software studio in Buenos Aires.
We just signed with Acme Logistics. I'm leading the go-live of their new billing system on Friday, December 11.
The cutover happens on-site at Acme's office in Córdoba, and I have to be there in person to run it.
My manager is Martín. He wants a status update every Monday morning.
Acme's project sponsor is Carolina, their CFO.
The contract says the old billing system gets switched off the same day as the go-live.
I prefer short meetings: 25 minutes at most, and never on Friday afternoons.
The billing system uses PostgreSQL 16 for the invoice ledger.
We picked Hangfire for the nightly invoice batch jobs.
Acme's invoices need a QR code for the tax authority.
Carolina wants a one-page summary of the project every week.
The tax rules module has to support three provinces at launch.
We plan two-week sprints, starting on Mondays.
I'm preparing a risk register for the project.
The first sprint planning went smoothly.
I bought a new standing desk for the home office.
Priya joined my team as our database engineer.
Priya will run the data migration the night before the go-live.
Tomás is our QA lead. He owns the regression test suite for the billing system.
Valentina is our frontend developer; she is building the invoice review screen.
For documentation I like checklists better than long documents.
We do our daily standup at 9:30, on video, fifteen minutes.
I drink mate all day, so please never schedule me a coffee chat.
Our planning meetings happen every second Monday.
I want the release plan to have a freeze window before every deploy.
Tomás proposed adding contract tests for the invoice API.
Valentina prefers Figma for the UI mockups.
Priya wants a dry run of the data migration on a copy of production.
We will prepare a demo for Acme at the end of October.
The project wiki lives in Confluence.
I started running three times a week before work.
My favourite series right now is a Spanish crime drama.
The go-live checklist has three gates: load test passed, rollback rehearsed, and finance sign-off.
The finance sign-off comes from Carolina.
The load test for the billing system is scheduled for November 18.
We will rehearse the rollback on November 25 with Priya and Tomás.
The staging environment for the billing system runs on Azure, in the Brazil South region.
Acme wants the invoices in Spanish and in English.
The billing system has to import about 40,000 historical invoices.
The migration dry run took nine hours; Priya wants to bring it under six.
We need to prepare user guides for the billing clerks.
Acme's IT team asked for the go-live plan in writing.
Carolina asked for a weekly status email on Fridays.
I prefer to review pull requests in the morning.
We added feature flags for the new invoice screens.
Martín wants the go-live plan reviewed by the architecture board.
I need to book a room for the go-live retrospective.
Nico and I are thinking about adopting a cat.
We moved the backlog from Trello to Azure Boards.
Diego will give us VPN access to Acme's network.
The invoice PDFs are generated with QuestPDF.
Tomás set up nightly regression runs at 2 am.
I want a short checklist for every deploy.
We need a plan B if the tax rules module slips.
Acme's accountants work until 6 pm, so deploys happen after that.
The weekly team lunch is on Wednesdays.
I finished the book about Patagonia.
The invoice import module is done; the tax rules module is still in progress.
Valentina finished the invoice review screen and Acme liked the demo.
We use GitHub Actions for CI and we deploy to Azure Container Apps.
Martín asked me to mentor Valentina on system design.
I'd like to give a talk about billing migrations at a meetup next year.
Our sprint reviews are every other Thursday at 4 pm.
Next sprint focuses on the tax rules module.
I want each week's priorities written down on Monday morning.
We need a war room at Acme during the go-live week.
Priya will prepare SQL scripts to verify the migrated totals.
Valentina will prepare a short video tutorial for the clerks.
Acme wants a hotline for invoice questions in the first week after the go-live.
The load test plan covers 1,000 invoices per minute.
I'm prepping a talk outline about billing migrations.
We celebrated Valentina's birthday with cake.
Acme asked for a training session for their billing clerks before the go-live.
I scheduled the training session for December 3: remote, two hours.
The go-live runbook needs a communication plan for Acme's customers.
Priya estimates the data migration will take about six hours.
We agreed on a code freeze for the billing system starting December 4.
Tomás wants one more full regression run after the code freeze.
The go-live support rota needs two people on call for the weekend after the cutover.
Some personal news: my sister Lucía is getting married!
The wedding is in Bariloche on Saturday, December 12. I already booked my flights: I will be in Bariloche from December 9 to December 13.
I'm reading a book about the history of Patagonia.
My partner Nico is vegetarian, keep that in mind for restaurant ideas.
I want to learn to make a proper chocolate fondue.
The readiness review checklist has twelve items.
Tomás wants to freeze the test data before the go-live.
We need printed runbooks for the cutover night.
Carolina will approve the go-live after the finance sign-off.
I prefer to plan the week on Sunday evenings.
Diego asked for the list of people who need building access.
The rollback plan needs Martín's sign-off.
Priya's migration scripts are now idempotent.
I signed up for a pottery class on Thursdays.
The load test passed: 1,200 invoices per minute, above the 1,000 target.
Tomás found two bugs in the tax rounding; both are fixed now.
Martín approved the go-live budget, including weekend support.
I still need to write the go-live runbook and the rollback checklist.
The billing system's monitoring dashboards are ready in Grafana.
We prepared a FAQ for Acme's billing clerks.
The go-live communication email is drafted.
Tomás will run a final smoke test after the cutover.
Valentina fixed the last accessibility issues on the review screen.
We need snacks for the cutover night.
The support rota spreadsheet is in the shared drive.
I want a 15-minute check-in every day of the go-live week.
Martín will join the go-live kickoff call remotely.
Nico is cooking empanadas this weekend.
The rollback rehearsal went well: 40 minutes to restore the old billing system.
Acme's IT contact for the cutover is Diego; he will open the office for us on go-live day.
I want the go-live day to start at 7 am with a short kickoff call.
Valentina will be on call with Tomás the weekend after the go-live.
After the go-live I want to take a few days off.
The monitoring alerts are routed to the on-call phone.
Acme confirmed the cutover window starts at 6 pm.
I need to print the go-live checklist.
Priya will be on site for the migration night.
We dropped the PDF batch job from the first release.
Carolina wants a summary after the first week of live invoicing.
Tomás finished the final regression run.
I renewed my passport.
The team voted for a celebration dinner after the go-live.
I booked a hotel in Córdoba near Acme's office.
The rental car pickup is at Córdoba airport.
Valentina will monitor the invoice queue remotely.
We need a backup laptop for the cutover.
Diego sent the building access badges.
The go-live readiness review passed.
I want the kickoff call agenda to fit on one page.
Acme's CFO will visit the war room.
Nico gave me a new thermos for mate.
